desc_p1: "Child of the Dark: Diary of a Favela Woman" is the visceral and poetic account by Carolina Maria de Jesus of her life in the Canindé favela in São Paulo.
desc_p2: Written between 1955 and 1960, the diary records with brutal honesty the hunger, poverty and daily struggle for survival.
desc_p3: The work became a publishing phenomenon, translated into over 13 languages and recognised as one of the most important testimonies of Brazilian literature.
analysis_p1: Child of the Dark, by Carolina Maria de Jesus, is an autobiographical diary that provides a direct and powerful view of life in the Canindé favela in São Paulo during the 1950s.
vest_lead: Understand the literary work through interpretation, social criticism and essay themes.
essay_topic1: The social invisibility of marginalized populations.
essay_topic2: Obstacles to guaranteeing human rights in Brazil.
vest_default_title: The Dual Perspective: Carolina vs. the Reader

char_desc_0: Narrator and protagonist. A Black woman, paper collector and single mother living in the Canindé favela in São Paulo. She is observant, critical and deeply aware of social inequality. Her writing works as resistance and denunciation.
char_desc_1: Carolina's son. Portrayed as rebellious and difficult to control, often involved in common conflicts that show the difficulties of motherhood under extreme poverty.
char_desc_2: Another son, usually described as more sensitive and obedient. The author shows concern for his nutrition, education and future.
char_desc_3: Youngest daughter of Carolina. Represents innocence and hope; Carolina often expresses the desire to give her a better life.
char_desc_4: Although many appear briefly, they form a collective character representing solidarity among the poor, conflicts caused by misery, violence, alcoholism and disputes, and the daily struggle for survival.
char_desc_5: Appear indirectly and critically; Carolina denounces empty promises, social abandonment and corruption. They symbolize public neglect towards the poor.

inicio_section_desc: The book is a real and impactful testimony to urban misery in Brazil, while revealing the strength, dignity and hope of a woman who finds writing as a form of resistance.
author_info: Carolina Maria de Jesus was a Brazilian writer, paper collector and favela resident who became famous after publishing Child of the Dark: Diary of a Favela Woman, which recounts poverty and social inequality in Brazil.
author_life: Carolina Maria de Jesus achieved global success with Child of the Dark (Quarto de Despejo, 1960), translated into over 14 languages and published in more than 40 countries. She became the most widely read Brazilian author abroad at the time. Beyond this bestseller, she left a broad literary legacy including Casa de Alvenaria, Pedaços da Fome, Provérbios, and Diário de Bitita. Today, she is celebrated as one of the most essential Black and social voices in Brazilian history.

frases.texto: Hunger is the dynamite of the human body.
Brazil needs to be led by someone who has already experienced hunger.
The dizziness caused by hunger is worse than that caused by alcohol. Alcohol makes us want to sing, but hunger makes us tremble.
Life is like a book. Only after it has been read do we know what it contains.
I came to the conclusion that those who do not need to go to heaven do not need to look up.
When I arrive in the city, I feel as though I am in paradise. Everything seems wonderful. But when I return to the favela, I feel like a discarded object.
There are days when I suffer so much that it seems I am the root of all the suffering in the world.
The cost of living is what revolts us. The cost of living is what turns us into victims.
